output.summary:
KEP-2718 proposed a client exec proxy extension to Kubernetes client libraries so that a client-side proxy process, configured solely from kubeconfig, could modify requests (e.g. request signing, hardware-protected mTLS keys) before they reach the API server. The KEP was withdrawn at alpha stage on 2024-07-05.</summary>
<parameter name="rationale">Existing client auth mechanisms (exec credential plugins, static tokens/certs, external HTTP proxies via environment variables) cannot easily sign whole requests, and running and securing an external proxy is operationally poor. The design went through many review rounds in PR #2693, where the reviewer enj rejected the proposed API structure and asked for an extension of ExecCredentialStatus instead. The sources do not record the reason for the eventual withdrawal.

alternatives.option: Keep the proposed standalone exec proxy config (ExecProxyConfig in ExecConfig, or a per-user proxy field in kubeconfig)
alternatives.why_not: enj disagreed with the structure: "I disagree with effectively the entire structure of this API. I expect this to be an extension to the existing client-go credential plugin API, specifically as extension to `ExecCredentialStatus`."

alternatives.option: Use an existing HTTP proxy via HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY environment variables or kubeconfig proxy URL
alternatives.why_not: The proposal says this "is not ideal for a generic request signing solution across all client configurations" because it needs a long running external proxy process and adds operational complexity.

alternatives.option: Keep UDS only and drop Windows alternatives
alternatives.why_not: Discussion ended with unnamed pipes added as a third alternative with the final choice deferred to implementation, so no single socket type was fixed in the design.

evidence.quote: The problem with this solution is that the operator experience of setting up and managing an external proxy is poor.
